purpose: Determine whether the large c2 changes across fixed C_tes anchors are mostly a parameter-coordinate effect or correspond to materially different normalized Magnicon+c2 readout transfer shapes.
guardrail: This diagnostic compares effective normalized readout-transfer shapes implied by each externally fixed C_tes assumption. A large anchor dependence means c2 is not quantitatively identifiable without stronger C_tes information; it does not by itself prove that the residual is detector-side rather than readout-side. Rows where c2 hits its configured bound are censored and excluded from the primary finite-shape classification.
